profile.name: Curran Stikuts
profile.bio: Toronto Centre community leader with 15+ years working in the ward — began in co-operative housing in the Downtown East, then community health; spent over a decade at The 519 Community Centre leading advocacy and community programs, and has served on foundation and social-policy boards.

promises.text: Push for more affordable homes, including housing with on-site support.
Help nonprofits buy rental buildings and turn unsold condos into affordable housing.
Allow sixplexes citywide.
Fight to double the Rent Bank.
Help tenants facing eviction.
Make landlords fix unsafe buildings.
Safer shelters and 24/7 spaces where people can come indoors while we help them find permanent homes.
Support a weekly TTC fare cap of ten paid rides, including for post-secondary students, with no upfront pass purchase.
Expand free recreation programs and add spaces so more people can swim, play sports and stay active.
Expand crisis teams.
Focus police resources on violence, threats and trafficking, with more neighbourhood officers on foot and bike.
Better lighting, regular cleaning, community programming and visible TTC staff.
Buses and streetcars at least every 15 minutes from 6 a.m. to 2 a.m., with shorter waits on busy routes.
Traffic signals that give transit priority.
Close local gaps in bike lanes.
Increase Bike Share funding so bikes and docks are available where needed.
Better construction coordination and limits on prolonged lane closures.
Faster road and sidewalk repairs.
Fund community organizations that support people targeted by hate.
Make it easier to report hate incidents and get help.

expensesDetailSource.name: Council Expense Routine Disclosure — Constituency Services & Office Expenses
expensesDetailSource.publisher: City Clerk's Office, City of Toronto
expensesDetailSource.note: Figures are the City's routine disclosure of constituency services and office expenses, shown as published, by category, from 2013. This is a separate publication from the annual remuneration reports in expenses.json, with a narrower scope — office spending only, not pay, benefits or staff salaries — and the two are never added together. Amounts shown as personal funds are the member's own money, as the City reports it. Invoice-level documents stay on the City's site; category amounts link to them.
